texts.orig: where I dissected the ten jobs of a product manager—based on reviewing 20+ PM career ladders at some of today’s biggest tech companies—in this post I’m going to share my favorite interview questions for PMs, one question per PM “job”. You don’t need to cover all ten questions in one session (i.e. you can split them across interviewers), and you may need to screen for fewer (or more!) areas based on the expectations of PMs at your company. My advice to you is to use this collection as inspiration and tailor your questions to your own needs.
texts.text: where I dissected the ten jobs of a product manager—based on reviewing 20+ PM career ladders at some of today’s biggest tech companies—in this post I’m going to share my favorite interview questions for PMs, one question per PM “job”. You don’t need to cover all ten questions in one session (i.e. you can split them across interviewers), and you may need to screen for fewer (or more!) areas based on the expectations of PMs at your company. My advice to you is to use this collection as inspiration and tailor your questions to your own needs.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In addition to ten PM-specific questions, I’ve also included my favorite generalist interview questions, no matter the function. I always try to find time to ask at least a couple of these questions.
texts.text: In addition to ten PM-specific questions, I’ve also included my favorite generalist interview questions, no matter the function. I always try to find time to ask at least a couple of these questions.

texts.orig: What’s the most important or impactful product you shipped? What made it so important or impactful?
texts.text: What’s the most important or impactful product you shipped? What made it so important or impactful?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Have they actually launched something significant, and how significant was it
texts.text: Have they actually launched something significant, and how significant was it

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: How do they measure impact/importance, and does it match your definition
texts.text: How do they measure impact/importance, and does it match your definition

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: How much responsibility they had in the project, or were they just helping out
texts.text: How much responsibility they had in the project, or were they just helping out

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: The example they pick is not very important—likely means they haven’t worked on anything meaty
texts.text: The example they pick is not very important—likely means they haven’t worked on anything meaty

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: They didn’t have much influence over what it was, or how it turned out
texts.text: They didn’t have much influence over what it was, or how it turned out

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Tell me about a time you disagreed with an engineer on your team, and how you resolved it.
texts.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with an engineer on your team, and how you resolved it.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Being able to convince others with information while also preserving relationships for the long term.
texts.text: Being able to convince others with information while also preserving relationships for the long term.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Genuinely hearing out the other person’s point of view—understanding their needs and priorities. And ideally, being convinced otherwise.
texts.text: Genuinely hearing out the other person’s point of view—understanding their needs and priorities. And ideally, being convinced otherwise.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Working backward from an outcome both parties want to achieve
texts.text: Working backward from an outcome both parties want to achieve

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Them backing down immediately, without a great reason
texts.text: Them backing down immediately, without a great reason

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Railroading the other person with their idea
texts.text: Railroading the other person with their idea

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Share a time you shipped a product that failed. Why did it fail and what did you learn?
texts.text: Share a time you shipped a product that failed. Why did it fail and what did you learn?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Can you give me one other example?
texts.text: Can you give me one other example?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Being able to identify and articulate the source of the failure
texts.text: Being able to identify and articulate the source of the failure

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Taking away a lesson that informs how they build product today
texts.text: Taking away a lesson that informs how they build product today

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Tell me about a time when your team didn’t gel. What was the issue, and how did you deal with it?
texts.text: Tell me about a time when your team didn’t gel. What was the issue, and how did you deal with it?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Has this happened on other teams you’ve been on?
texts.text: Has this happened on other teams you’ve been on?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Taking it upon themselves to solve this problem—a history of spending time and energy on improving team dynamics
texts.text: Taking it upon themselves to solve this problem—a history of spending time and energy on improving team dynamics

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Being able to articulate the root cause of the issue
texts.text: Being able to articulate the root cause of the issue

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A pattern of teams they’ve been on not gelling
texts.text: A pattern of teams they’ve been on not gelling

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pick a project you’re proud of that took 3-9 months. Walk me through it from beginning to end. I’ll ask questions along the way. [Give this ~7-10 mins]
texts.text: Pick a project you’re proud of that took 3-9 months. Walk me through it from beginning to end. I’ll ask questions along the way. [Give this ~7-10 mins]

texts.label: text
texts.orig: What to look for (and dig into):
texts.text: What to look for (and dig into):

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: How they aligned around the priorities, success criteria, and a timeline
texts.text: How they aligned around the priorities, success criteria, and a timeline

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: How they dealt with delays and disagreements—how efficiently and effectively they got work back on track
texts.text: How they dealt with delays and disagreements—how efficiently and effectively they got work back on track

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: How they kept everyone aligned and focused throughout
texts.text: How they kept everyone aligned and focused throughout

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: How they kept their manager/execs onboard
texts.text: How they kept their manager/execs onboard

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: They were told what to build and they just built it
texts.text: They were told what to build and they just built it

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: There were zero issues, which almost never happens and probably means they aren’t being honest
texts.text: There were zero issues, which almost never happens and probably means they aren’t being honest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pick a product you worked on in the past year—talk me through your product strategy for it.
texts.text: Pick a product you worked on in the past year—talk me through your product strategy for it.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: [Alternatively] A take-home assignment to come up with a strategy to 10x the growth of your existing product.
texts.text: [Alternatively] A take-home assignment to come up with a strategy to 10x the growth of your existing product.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Excitement to talk about this, body language, and energy
texts.text: Excitement to talk about this, body language, and energy

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A clear, succinct, and cohesive articulation of the strategy
texts.text: A clear, succinct, and cohesive articulation of the strategy

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Deep insights into the problem they were solving
texts.text: Deep insights into the problem they were solving

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: It’s hard to follow their strategy
texts.text: It’s hard to follow their strategy

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Tell me about a time you did user research on a product/feature, and that research had a big impact on the product.
texts.text: Tell me about a time you did user research on a product/feature, and that research had a big impact on the product.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Examples of them talking to customers before launch
texts.text: Examples of them talking to customers before launch

texts.text: These conversations impacting what they launch

texts.text: Experience using different modes of research (e.g. survey, 1:1 conversations)

texts.orig: Haven’t spent time talking to customers
texts.text: Haven’t spent time talking to customers

texts.text: It’s hard for them to think of an example

texts.text: Tell me the vision for one of your recent projects or teams.

texts.orig: They actually have a vision to share
texts.text: They actually have a vision to share

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: They get excited about sharing their vision
texts.text: They get excited about sharing their vision

texts.text: The vision they share is at least somewhat inspiring

texts.text: They only share the impact they plan to drive, or a set of features, versus a vision of the future

texts.orig: They can’t think of any examples
texts.text: They can’t think of any examples

texts.orig: How do you get your team to commit to a deadline?
texts.text: How do you get your team to commit to a deadline?

texts.text: Working with their teammates to co-create deadlines
